Subject: Procurement question — marketplace listing vs direct MSA for NimbusHealth

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited about Redwood's latency profile. Procurement is currently triaging the best way for us to purchase: via AWS Marketplace private offer, or sign a direct MSA + Redwood invoice. Two questions they asked that I couldn't answer off the cuff:

1) If we buy through AWS Marketplace (private offer), who ends up being the seller-of-record for billing and who issues the invoice (AWS or Redwood)?
2) If we go direct with a Redwood invoice under our PO and signed MSA, do we lose any co-sell credits or partner incentives that come from a marketplace purchase?

We've attached our standard PO template for reference. Procurement would also like to understand timelines — Marketplace private-offer approvals can add a couple weeks. Can you outline the tradeoffs and recommended path for a regulated healthcare buyer?

Subject: Re: Procurement question — marketplace listing vs direct MSA for NimbusHealth

Hi Alice — great questions, thanks for sending the PO template. Quick summary up front: both paths are viable; the decision typically comes down to (1) invoice ownership & tax handling, (2) speed of procurement/approval, and (3) whether you need marketplace-specific co-sell incentives.

High-level differences:
- AWS Marketplace (Private Offer): AWS is usually the bill-to (seller/merchant of record depends on offer config). You receive an AWS invoice; Redwood receives payment via AWS. Private offers can map cost center lines to AWS SKUs and enable certain AWS co-sell programs. Time to close can be longer because of marketplace offer setup and approvals; however, for customers who require marketplace procurement or want consolidated cloud spend, it's often preferred.

- Direct MSA + Redwood Invoice: Redwood is seller-of-record, we invoice directly and you pay Redwood. Faster from a contract/legal perspective in many cases; flexible invoicing (monthly/quarterly). Co-sell incentives may need to be handled via an existing partner agreement between Redwood and AWS (we can register the deal for co-sell), but the mechanics differ — incentives are typically tracked off-invoice.

For regulated healthcare (PHI considerations), the main operational points:
- Private Offer does not change data residency or the technical deployment; those are determined by the SKU/deployment choice and your security requirements.
- If you need an on-prem/VPC Private deployment contractually tied to your MSA, direct contracting sometimes simplifies SLAs and onboarding obligations.

I'll loop in Kimberly for the finer points on seller-of-record and any Marketplace SKUs that would apply, and Lauren to propose the next steps and a recommended timeline.

Best,
Marcus
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Hi Alice — adding the marketplace mechanics and Seller-of-Record (SOR) detail: 

1) Seller-of-Record & invoice flow (typical setups):
   - AWS as SOR: AWS issues the invoice to the customer; Redwood receives payment from AWS. This is common when Redwood lists a product in AWS Marketplace and sets up a SaaS private offer where AWS handles billing. Your finance team will see an AWS invoice and reconcile against AWS spend.
   - Redwood as SOR: Redwood invoices NimbusHealth directly (our current standard). We issue invoices that match your PO lines.

2) Co-sell credits & incentives:
   - Purchasing via Marketplace can make some co-sell incentives cleaner from the AWS channel perspective because the transaction is visible in AWS systems and can be associated with partner programs automatically.
   - Direct purchases can still be co-sell eligible; we typically register the opportunity with AWS PS and capture credits via the partner registration process. That path requires some post-sale registration and occasionally manual crediting.

3) Recommended for NimbusHealth (regulated buyer):
   - If procurement requires a consolidated cloud spend and uses AWS invoices exclusively: go marketplace private offer.
   - If you need Redwood to be contractually accountable for onboarding and specific contract terms (e.g., data processing addendum tied to our MSA), direct MSA may be simpler and faster.

Note on timing: setting up a private offer and aligning SKUs and pricing typically takes ~7–14 business days (could be longer if a custom procurement/legal review with AWS is required). If you want to pursue both in parallel (start the private offer while signing an interim direct MSA), we can do that — provides the fastest path to production without blocking procurement.

Happy to jump on a short call with your procurement and AWS rep to walk the team through invoice samples and required paperwork.

Kimberly Park
Head of Channel & Cloud Partnerships, Redwood Inference
